we can use high-content screening to measure phenotypes in cells that are relevant to human diseases and use the data to discover new drugs.

the discovery of novel chemical probes and drug leads for targets in a number of disease areas.
the discovery of novel therapeutic targets and the development of new technologies to facilitate the discovery process.
the discovery of new chemical entities (NCEs) that are efficacious in the clinic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future of drug discovery is empirical.

empirical drug discovery is an important and valuable approach to drug discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we use high-throughput screening to identify small molecules that perturb the proteome.
we have demonstrated that phenotypic drug screening is a valid and effective approach to the identification and validation of new drug targets.
we have developed an approach for the discovery of novel small molecule inhibitors of the protease domain of the human proteasome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are now able to identify the most promising targets and compounds for a given disease by integrating the phenotypic data from a wide range of cellular systems and assays.
the use of complex cellular systems for drug discovery can be very powerful, and that the field is still at a very early stage in the development of this approach.
